8	/-!
9	# CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST: `isOpen_chartLocus`, and the advertised lemma that did not exist
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean` proves `isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` over an
12	**affine** test, and its docstring says the general-test statement "follows from this one by the
13	affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s transport (iii) … needs no new mathematics".  That
14	claim is right, and this file discharges it — but two of its ingredients were not where the tree
15	said they were.
16	
17	## The advertised lemma that was absent
18	
19	`Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`'s header says chart-independence of the residue field is free
20	"and the chart comparison becomes a lemma (`testPointField_affineOpen_iso`) instead of a side
21	condition.  That is the whole reason this file is short."  **No declaration of that name exists
22	anywhere in the workspace** — the only occurrence was that sentence (cf. I-0624:
23	advertised-but-absent).  Since it is cited as the reason a side condition is unnecessary, it is
24	load-bearing prose, so it is supplied here as `testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso`.
25	
26	It is genuinely cheap, but not for the reason the header gives: what makes it work is that
27	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U` is an **open immersion** on carriers
28	(`IsAffineOpen.isOpenImmersion_fromSpec`), and mathlib already knows the residue-field map of an
29	open immersion is an isomorphism
30	(`Scheme.instIsIsoCommRingCatResidueFieldMapOfIsOpenImmersion`).  So the comparison is an
31	iso for a structural reason, not by a computation with `Spec.residueFieldIso`.
32	
33	## Locality: what "open in every affine piece" needs
34	
35	`isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open`-style bookkeeping is not quite enough, because the locus over the
36	piece is a subset of a *different* space (`Spec Γ(T.left, U)`, not `T.left`).  The bridge is that
37	`fromSpecAffine`'s carrier map is an open immersion with range `U`, so the image of the piece's
38	locus is the intersection of `chartLocus` with `U` — that is what
39	`chartLocus_inter_affineOpen_eq_image` records, and the openness statement then follows from
40	openness of an open immersion's image.
41	
42	## Main declarations
43	
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso` — **the absent advertised lemma**:
45	  the residue-field comparison along an affine-open test object is an isomorphism.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff` — hence the split-witness predicate
47	  at a point of an affine piece agrees with the one at its image in `T`; this is transport (i)'s
48	  hypothesis `hinv` **discharged** for the affine-piece maps (both directions), rather than
49	  assumed.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` — **CHART-U(b) at a general test**: if
51	  `chartLocus` is open over each affine-open test object, it is open over `T`.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_presentations` — the same fed with the per-piece
53	  presentation hypotheses, i.e. the general-test keystone of dat-b row B-4 modulo exactly the
54	  per-piece shifted-datum presentations and nothing else.
55	-/
56

72	/- The section ring of an affine open is a `k`-algebra; `PicEtUnit.lean` declares this as a
73	LOCAL instance, so every file stating something about `overSpec k Γ(T.left, U)` must re-open it. -/
74	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
75	
76	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
77	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
78	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
79	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
80	
81	noncomputable section

83	namespace Over
84	
85	/-! ## The absent advertised lemma -/
86	
87	/-- **The residue-field comparison along an affine-open test object is an isomorphism** — the
88	lemma `Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`'s header advertises as `testPointField_affineOpen_iso`
89	and which does not exist under that (or any) name.
90	
91	For `U` an affine open of `T.left` and `t` a point of `Spec Γ(T.left, U)`, the induced extension
92	`κ(fromSpecAffine T U (t)) → κ(t)` is invertible.
93	
94	The reason is structural rather than computational: `IsAffineOpen.fromSpec` is an open immersion,
95	and the residue-field map of an open immersion is an iso in mathlib already. -/
96	instance testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
97	    (U : T.left.affineOpens) (t : (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)).left) :
98	    IsIso (testPointFieldMap (fromSpecAffine T U) t) := by
99	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (fromSpecAffine T U).left := U.2.isOpenImmersion_fromSpec
100	  exact Scheme.instIsIsoCommRingCatResidueFieldMapOfIsOpenImmersion
101	    (fromSpecAffine T U).left t
102	
103	end Over
104	
105	/-! ## Transport (i) for the affine-piece maps, both directions -/
106	
107	variable (C) in
108	/-- **The residue-field-iso invariance of the split-witness predicate** — the obligation the
109	general-test assembly actually rests on, named rather than hidden.
110	
111	`mem_chartLocus_of_mem_chartLocus_comp` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:360`) says transport (i) "proves
112	nothing on its own — it is an interface, and its proof is `hinv`", and that the tree's landed
113	invariance discharges `hinv` for *separable* residue-field extensions.  For an affine-open test
114	object the extension is an **isomorphism** (`Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso` — hence in
115	particular separable), so morally transport (i) is free here.
116	
117	**But the landed invariance is about `HasWitnessH1Vanishing`, not about `IsSplitWitness`**, and no
118	declaration in the tree transports `IsSplitWitness` along a field isomorphism: measured, the only
119	mentions of `IsSplitWitness` invariance are two docstring sentences.  So the affine-piece case of
120	transport (i) needs *one* lemma the tree does not have, which is this predicate.  That is a
121	correction to `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s claim that the general-test statement "needs no new
122	mathematics": it needs exactly this, and nothing else.
123	
124	Why it is believable and small: `IsSplitWitness C μ` is an existential over a finite separable
125	`L/K` presenting `μ`.  Along an isomorphism `K ≃ K'` the same `L` presents the transported class,
126	because `PicEtAff.map` composes (`PicEtAff.map_map`) and the inverse iso undoes the transport —
127	i.e. it is `map_map` plus `map_id`, not geometry.  It is stated as a class-free hypothesis here so
128	that the assembly below is usable the moment a lane proves it. -/
129	def IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant : Prop :=
130	  ∀ (T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))) (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left)
131	    (_ : IsIso (Over.testPointFieldMap f t)) (mu : picEt C T),
132	      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (picEtMap C f mu))
133	        ↔ IsSplitWitness C
134	            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)) mu)
135	
136	variable (C) in
137	/-- **The split-witness predicate agrees along an affine-open test object**, given the
138	iso-invariance.
139	
140	This is transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6 for the affine-piece maps, in **both** directions — so
141	the locus over the piece and the locus over `T` correspond exactly, which is what the locality
142	assembly needs (a one-sided containment would not give openness).
143	
144	The only input beyond landed material is `hinv`; the `IsIso` it is applied at is discharged by
145	`Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso`, i.e. structurally, by mathlib's fact that an open
146	immersion induces an isomorphism of residue fields. -/
147	theorem isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
148	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) (mu : picEt C T)
149	    (t : (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)).left) :
150	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t)
151	        (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) mu))
152	      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C
153	          (Over.testPoint (T := T) ((Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base t)) mu) :=
154	  hinv T (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) t
155	    (Over.testPointField_fromSpecAffine_isIso T U t) mu
156	
157	/-! ## Locality: the general-test assembly -/
158	
159	variable (C) in
160	/-- **The affine piece's locus is the preimage of the general-test locus.**
161	
162	For an affine open `U ⊆ T.left`, `chartLocus` over the affine test object `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` is
163	the preimage, along the carrier map of `Over.fromSpecAffine T U`, of `chartLocus` over `T`.
164	
165	Both sides unfold to the same split-witness condition read at two residue fields, so this is
166	`isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff` applied pointwise together with `picEtMap_chartTwist` (the
167	twist commutes with restriction). -/
168	theorem chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
169	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
170	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.affineOpens) (lam : picEt C T) :
171	    chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)
172	      = (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base ⁻¹' chartLocus C m Z lam := by
173	  refine Set.ext fun t => ?_
174	  rw [Set.mem_preimage, mem_chartLocus_iff, mem_chartLocus_iff,
175	    ← picEtMap_chartTwist]
176	  exact isSplitWitness_fromSpecAffine_iff C hinv T U (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t
177	
178	variable (C) in
179	/-- **CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST**, i.e. the statement `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring
180	promises follows from the affine case "by the affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s
181	transport (iii)".
182	
183	If `chartLocus` is open over every affine-open test object of `T`, it is open over `T`.
184	
185	The bookkeeping is genuinely bookkeeping — but note *which* bookkeeping, because it is not the
186	`isOpen_iff_forall_isOpen_inter` the docstring names: the piece's locus lives in a **different
187	space** (`Spec Γ(T.left, U)`, not `T.left`), so the bridge is that the carrier map is an open
188	immersion whose range is `U` (`IsAffineOpen.range_fromSpec`).  The preimage identity
189	`chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage` then turns per-piece openness into openness of
190	`chartLocus ∩ U`, and the affine opens cover `T.left`. -/
191	theorem isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal (hinv : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C)
192	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
193	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
194	    (haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
195	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))) :
196	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z lam) := by
197	  -- Openness is local: it suffices that every point of the locus has an open neighbourhood
198	  -- inside it, and each point lies in some affine open of `T.left`.
199	  rw [isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open]
200	  intro t ht
201	  -- an affine open around `t`
202	  obtain ⟨U, hUmem⟩ : ∃ U : T.left.affineOpens, t ∈ U.1 := by
203	    obtain ⟨U, hU, hmem, -⟩ :=
204	      (TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp T.left.isBasis_affineOpens)
205	        (show t ∈ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) from trivial)
206	    exact ⟨⟨U, hU⟩, hmem⟩
207	  -- the piece's locus is open, and its image is `chartLocus ∩ U`
208	  have hpre := chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage C hinv m Z T U lam
209	  refine ⟨chartLocus C m Z lam ∩ U.1, Set.inter_subset_left, ?_, ht, hUmem⟩
210	  -- `chartLocus ∩ U` is the image of the piece's locus under an open immersion with range `U`
211	  have hoi : IsOpenImmersion (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left := U.2.isOpenImmersion_fromSpec
212	  have hrange : Set.range (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base = (U.1 : Set T.left) := by
213	    change Set.range (U.2.fromSpec).base = _
214	    exact U.2.range_fromSpec
215	  have himg : (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base ''
216	        (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))
217	      = chartLocus C m Z lam ∩ U.1 := by
218	    rw [hpre, Set.image_preimage_eq_inter_range, hrange]
219	  rw [← himg]
220	  haveI := hoi
221	  exact (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.isOpenEmbedding.isOpenMap _ (haff U)
222	
223	end
224	
225	end AlgebraicGeometry

100	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
101	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
102	
103	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
104	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
105	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
106	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
107	
108	noncomputable section
109	
110	/-! ## The split witness predicate at a class over a field -/
111	
112	variable (C) in
113	/-- **The split witness predicate** (CHART-U(a) in the `w4-datb` §1.6 (a-amendment)
114	spelling), at a plus class `μ` over a field `K`.
115	
116	A plus class over a field need not be an honest Čech class — it is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for
117	an étale cover `E` of `K`.  The amendment's "for some finite separable `L/κ(t)` splitting
118	the collapsed plus class" is this: there is a finite separable extension `L/K` over which
119	`μ` becomes `relPicMk` of an honest Čech class `M` on `C_L`, and `M` admits an effective
120	witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`.
121	
122	Stated with the witness clause on a *presenting Čech class* rather than on a datum,
123	because the datum layer is where the shifted-datum constructor (DAT-C GAP-1) is missing;
124	the two agree through `Pic0ChartLocusClass.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.
125	
126	## A convention this predicate INHERITS, and which a consumer must not misread
127	
128	The worksheets say "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`".  The witness clause here —
129	and the tree's `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`
130	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`) that it mirrors, and the GAP-6 dictionary
131	`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (`DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:182`) that both rest
132	on — asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  It asks only for a `CurveDivisor` in the
133	class with vanishing `H¹`.  That is deliberate on the tree's side: the dictionary is an *iff*
134	against the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗ L)`, and that
135	condition cannot see effectivity or degree, so adding either clause would break the iff and
136	with it the openness route.
137	
138	Two consequences, both load-bearing:
139	
140	* the degree is supplied **externally**, by the chart-index constraint through
141	  `degAt_chartTwist` below: on a degree-zero `λ` the twisted class has fibre degree
142	  `m·d₁ − deg Z`, which the constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − g` makes `+g`.  It is *not* a
143	  hypothesis of this predicate.  (Until 2026-07-28 this read `−g`, and that sign made the
144	  locus empty for every `g ≥ 1` — see `degAt_chartTwist` and issue I-0514;
145	  `chartTwist_chartValue` now pins the direction by the kernel);
146	* effectivity likewise is not asserted here.  Where the *worksheet's* stronger reading is
147	  actually needed — the canonical-section normalization `h⁰ = 1`, and GAP-2 uniqueness
148	  (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`, which does take `0 ≤ D`, `0 ≤ D'`) — the
149	  effectivity must be re-supplied at that point.  A lane that reads `IsSplitWitness` as
150	  already giving it will have a gap where it least expects one. -/
151	def IsSplitWitness {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
152	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) : Prop :=
153	  ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
154	      (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
155	      (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic),
156	    PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
157	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
158	      ∧ ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
159	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
160	            ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
161	                ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)
162	
163	/-! ## The twisted fibre family -/
164	
165	variable (C) in
166	/-- **The twisted family whose chart-membership `chartLocus` tests**: the plus class `λ`
167	shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned θ-family.
168	
169	This is the *class-side* half of `chartValue` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`): where
170	`chartValue` twists the Abel class of a divisor family, `chartTwist` twists an arbitrary
171	plus class by the same two factors.  A point of `chartLocus` is precisely a point at which
172	`chartTwist` is realised by an effective divisor with no `H¹` — i.e. at which `λ` itself is
173	a chart value, after undoing the twist. -/
174	def chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
175	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : picEt C T :=
176	  lam * (thetaFamily C (thetaCechClass C) T ^ m) * (sigmaFamily C Z T)⁻¹
177	
178	/-- **The degree ledger of the twist**: at every field point the twisted family has fibre
179	degree `m·d₁ − deg Z` when `λ` is degree-zero.  With the chart-index constraint
180	`deg Z = m·d₁ − g` this is `+g`, which is the degree at which an effective witness with
181	`h¹ = 0` can exist at all.
182	
183	**Sign discipline, and it was wrong here until 2026-07-28 (issue I-0514).**  `chartTwist`
184	must be the INVERSE of `chartValue`'s twist, not the same one.  `chartValue` is
185	`abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` (`DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`), so recovering the Abel class from a chart
186	value means multiplying by `θᵐ` and dividing by `Σ` — hence `chartTwist` is
187	`λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`.  An earlier version applied the `chartValue` twist itself, giving fibre degree
188	`deg Z − m·d₁ = −g`; since `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))` forces `deg W ≥ g − 1`, that locus was
189	**empty for every `g ≥ 1`** and its openness was the openness of `∅`.  The comparison point is
190	`degAt_chartValue` at `n = g` (where the chart index is calibrated and `chartValue` lands in
191	`pic0`), NOT at `n = 0`.
192	
193	**An independent confirmation that `+g` is the right target**, worth recording because the
194	wrong sign survived two sessions: at `deg W = g` the rank anchor
195	`h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) gives, for a
196	witness with `h¹ = 0`,
197	`h⁰ = deg W + χ(𝒪) = g + (1 − g) = 1` — exactly the `h⁰ = 1` normalization that DAT-C §2 and
198	GAP-2's uniqueness both require.  So `+g` is not merely the sign that makes the locus nonempty;
199	it is the unique degree at which the witness is *unique*, which is what the chart map needs to be
200	injective.  At `−g` the same anchor gives `h⁰ = 1 − 2g`, negative for `g ≥ 1` — the contradiction
201	that made the locus empty. -/

274	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
275	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C L π) {M : (relCurve C L).CechPic}
276	    (hD : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) D.cechPicClass
277	      = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) M) :
278	    (∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
279	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) M
280	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
281	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1))
282	      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := by
283	  rw [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing, hD]

286	field** — the substantive half of the (a-amendment)'s "some (equivalently every)".
287	
288	If a Čech class `M` over `C_L` has an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`, then

293	Proof: present `M` by a datum `D` over `L` (`exists_cechPicClass_eq`); the witness clause at
294	`L` is `D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L`, which transfers to `L'` by the co-owned separable

296	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:157` — itself resting only on faithful flatness of a field
297	extension, so separability is packaging, not content). -/
298	theorem exists_witness_of_separable_extension (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
299	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
300	    {L' : Type u} [Field L'] [Algebra k L'] [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower k L L']
301	    [Algebra.IsSeparable L L'] (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
302	    (h : ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
303	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
304	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
305	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)) :
306	    ∃ W' : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L').left).CurveDivisor,
307	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L' W' = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L') M
308	        ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
309	            ((C ⊗ overSpec k L').left.divisorSheaf L' W') 1) := by
310	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (B := L) (π := π) M
311	  obtain ⟨W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
312	  -- the witness clause at `L` is the datum predicate at `L`: `relCurveMap C L L` acts as
313	  -- the identity comparison on classes, since it is `Spec` of the identity algebra map.
314	  have hid : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) D.cechPicClass = D.cechPicClass := by
315	    have : relCurveMap C L L = 𝟙 (relCurve C L) := by
316	      rw [relCurveMap]
317	      have hom : overSpecMap (k := k) L L = 𝟙 (overSpec k L) :=
318	        Over.OverMorphism.ext (by simp)
319	      rw [hom, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id]
320	      rfl
321	    rw [this, Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
322	    rfl
323	  have hL : D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := ⟨W, by rw [hid, hD, hW], hW1⟩
324	  -- transfer along the separable extension, then read it back as a witness clause
325	  obtain ⟨W', hW', hW1'⟩ :=
326	    (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable L L').mp hL
327	  exact ⟨W', by rw [hW', hD], hW1'⟩

332	`picEtMap`, so restricting `λ` along a morphism of tests restricts the twisted family too.

334	This is `sigmaFamily_natural` + `thetaFamily_natural` and nothing else; it is stated

337	theorem picEtMap_chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)

339	    picEtMap C f (chartTwist C m Z T lam)
340	      = chartTwist C m Z T' (picEtMap C f lam) := by
341	  rw [chartTwist, chartTwist, map_mul, map_inv, map_mul, map_pow,
342	    sigmaFamily_natural, thetaFamily_natural]

360	theorem mem_chartLocus_of_mem_chartLocus_comp (m : ℕ)

9	/-!
10	# Field points of a general test from points of its space — CHART-U(a) input 0
11	
12	`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3 freezes `chartLocus c λ` as a **subset of a general
13	test** `T`: a set of *points* `t : T.left`, at each of which one reads the fibre class of
14	`λ` at the residue field `κ(t)`.  `informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6 co-signs it and
15	lists three missing inputs (the shifted-datum constructor, the split predicate, the
16	descent/étale-image transports).
17	
18	**There is a fourth, prior to all three, and it is why nothing in the tree implements
19	`chartLocus`.**  The two vocabularies the definition has to join do not meet anywhere:
20	
21	* every witness/vanishing predicate in the tree is indexed by a prime of an **affine**
22	  base — `q : PrimeSpectrum B`, fibre field `q.asIdeal.ResidueField`
23	  (`Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean:80`, `Pic0ChartLocusClass.lean:82`,
24	  `DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:363`);
25	* every *class* is evaluated at a field point only through a **morphism**
26	  `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` for an abstract field `K` (`degAt`, `Pic0Functor.lean:54`;
27	  `pic0Subgroup`, `:107`).
28	
29	Nothing converts a point of `T.left` into either.  This file is that conversion, and it
30	is deliberately kept free of the chart layer: no `chartLocus`, no `θ`, no `Σ`, no
31	`divRep`.
32	
33	## Main declarations
34	
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPointField t` — the residue field `κ(t)` of a point of
36	  `T.left`, as a `k`-algebra (`Scheme.residueField`, with the `k`-algebra structure
37	  pulled back along the structure morphism).
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPoint t` — **the bridge**: the field point
39	  `overSpec k κ(t) ⟶ T` supported at `t`.  Built from mathlib's
40	  `Scheme.fromSpecResidueField`, whose triangle over `Spec k` is the `Over` datum.
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPoint_base` — it really is supported at `t`: the unique
42	  point of `Spec κ(t)` maps to `t`.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPoint_comp` — **naturality**, the law every well-definedness
44	  argument downstream runs on: for `f : T' ⟶ T` and `t : T'.left`, the field point of `t`
45	  followed by `f` is the field point of `f t`, up to the residue-field extension
46	  `κ(f t) → κ(t)` that `f` induces.  Stated as a commuting square rather than an equality
47	  of morphisms out of one object, because the two sides have different sources.
48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPointAffine` — the affine comparison: on `overSpec k A` the
49	  field point of a prime `q` is the residue-field point of `q`, so every affine-indexed
50	  predicate of the tree can be read through `testPoint`.
51	
52	## Why the affine-chart route is *not* the definition of record
53	
54	The obvious route (pick an affine open `U ∋ t`, use `q := U.2.primeIdealOf t` and
55	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U`, `PicEtUnit.lean:61`) needs a well-definedness lemma across the
56	choice of `U` before it can define anything.  Mathlib's `fromSpecResidueField` is already
57	canonical, so the chart-independence is *free* here and the chart comparison becomes a
58	lemma (`testPointField_affineOpen_iso`) instead of a side condition.  That is the whole
59	reason this file is short.
60	-/

129	      = (Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)).hom :=

142	  -- identity is the `Over` triangle of the affine test object: `(overSpec k A).hom` is by
143	  -- definition `Spec.map (algebraMap k A)`.
144	  have hcomp : ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t ≫ (overSpec k A).hom)

146	          ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)) := rfl
147	  -- `Spec.preimage` is injective on the composite, and the composite identity is `hcomp`.

150	        ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).hom
151	      = (algebraMap A (testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)).comp
152	          (algebraMap k A) := by

154	          ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))
155	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)
156	            ≫ Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)) := by
157	      rw [Spec.map_comp, Spec.map_preimage]
158	      rfl
159	    rw [this, Spec.preimage_map]
160	    rfl
161	  exact hw.trans hsplit

# Concurrent-lane protocol (2026-07-16, from inbox I-0149's incidents — BINDING for parallel agent fleets)

Adopted after the 2026-07-16 evening wave's four incidents (I-0149). These rules extend the
standing handoff protocol (07-14/14b/15) for any session running two or more lanes in this
workspace.

## 1. Ledger commits: private index + compare-and-swap (the shared-index race)

All lanes commit through one `workspace.git`; concurrent `git add`+`commit` through the
SHARED index can interleave and record spurious deletions of another lane's
freshly-committed files (happened in `6197c9676`, 862 lines vanished from HEAD, restored
byte-identical in `a640fef5b`). Concurrent lanes MUST commit via a private index:

```bash
cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)
COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD -c user.name="Archon Horizon" -c user.email="archon-horizon@local" \
  commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "<math-first message>

Archon-Commit: agent
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # CAS: fails if HEAD moved
unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
```

If the `update-ref` CAS fails (HEAD moved), re-read HEAD and repeat — never force.
ALWAYS verify afterward: `git --git-dir=$GD show --stat HEAD` must touch only your paths.
A single-lane session may keep the plain `add`+`commit` recipe, but must still verify.

### 1a. THE RECIPE ABOVE HAS A RACE — read HEAD ONCE, not twice (2026-07-28, run 0072)

**As written, the recipe reads `HEAD` twice**: once in `read-tree HEAD`, and again several lines
later in `PARENT=$(… rev-parse HEAD)`. If another lane's CAS lands **between those two reads**,
your tree is built from the *old* snapshot while your parent is the *new* commit — and
`update-ref` **succeeds**, because it only checks that the ref has not moved since `rev-parse`.
It never checks that the tree was built from that ref. You publish a stale tree, silently
reverting everything that landed in the window.

**Measured once, and the measurement is narrow — do not over-read it.** `e964967e8` has parent
`a1ef4d59c` and, diffed against *that parent*, deletes 95 lines of
`informal/w4-rep-critical-path.md`, 52 of `informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` and 19 of
`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean` — exactly the restore `a1ef4d59c` had just performed, undone.
Its `read-tree` ran before `a1ef4d59c` landed; its parent was captured after. It staged explicit
paths and the pathspec *was* honoured: **the sweep came from the TREE BASE, not the pathspec**,
which is why "stage explicit files" is not a defence and why the symptom is indistinguishable
from §1b's shared-index staleness.

**Two other lanes audited their own CAS commits the same day (fifteen commits between them,
recipe verbatim) and found zero reverts.** That is consistent with this: the race only fires when
another lane's CAS lands inside your particular window, so clean commits are the expected
outcome, not evidence of absence. The discriminating question is not "did my commits look clean"
but "was my `read-tree` separated from my `rev-parse` by somebody else's commit". Treat §1a as
cheap insurance, not as a diagnosis of every mystery revert — and check §1b too.

**The fix is one line — capture the parent BEFORE the tree, and read-tree that sha:**

```bash
PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)     # ONCE, up front
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree $PARENT      # not "HEAD"
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD … commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "…")
git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # now genuinely atomic
```

Then a mid-recipe CAS by another lane makes `update-ref` **fail**, you re-read and retry, and the
protocol behaves as it was meant to. The verification step ("must touch only your paths") is what
catches it after the fact — run it every time, and read the file list, not just the count.

### 1b. The CAS recipe leaves the SHARED index permanently stale — this is by design, and it is armed

Added 2026-07-27 (run 0048 r5) after this failed a **third** time (`I-0366`: the shared index
was pinned to a pre-round-5 snapshot and a bare `git commit` would have deleted
`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean` and un-rooted it from `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` in one commit).

The mechanism is not a bug in anyone's lane, it is the direct consequence of §1: a CAS commit
publishes a tree built in a **private** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and moves the ref with `update-ref`.
The **shared** index is never touched, so the moment anybody commits, the shared index still
describes the previous HEAD — and `git status` then reports that difference as *staged changes*,
including **staged deletions** for any file the commit added. The longer a run goes, the further
the shared index drifts behind.

Consequences, all three binding:

1. **Never run a bare `git commit` (no `-a`, no pathspec) against `workspace.git`.** It publishes
   whatever the stale shared index holds, which is a reversion of other lanes' work.
2. **Before finishing, check and repair.** `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. status --porcelain | grep '^D'`
   must be empty. If it is not, repair with the **narrowest** form that covers your paths:
   `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. reset -q -- <your project dir>/`. Prefer this to a whole-index
   `read-tree HEAD` when another run is live — a full reset can discard the other run's staging.
3. **Verify the worktree is the good copy before repairing.** `reset` makes the index match HEAD;
   that is only safe once you have confirmed the on-disk file is the one you want
   (`diff <(git --git-dir=$GD cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>`).

Expect to repeat step 2 more than once in a long session: every CAS commit by any lane re-stales
the index, so a repair done early does not stay done.

## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there

`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:

```bash
LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
    fi
    # No pidfile (old-cohort holder): reap only if NO live lake build AND the dir is >15 min old.
    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f 'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
       && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) )) -gt 900 ]; then
      echo "STALE: no live build, lock >15min old — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
    fi
  fi
  sleep 10
done
echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null      # record holder so a later reaper can prove liveness via kill -0
# … lake build … ; rm -rf "$LOCK"      # release (rm -rf, not rmdir — the pidfile makes the dir non-empty)
```

### 2a. THE RELEASE IS AS DANGEROUS AS THE REAP — check the pidfile before `rm -rf` (2026-07-28, run 0072)

The acquire loop above is careful; the release (`rm -rf "$LOCK"`) is not, and that asymmetry
caused a real incident. **A lane removed the lock directory while its pidfile named a LIVE pid
belonging to another lane's build**, having printed `ALIVE` for that pid one line earlier.

/-! ## The introduction rule COV-1 uses

Read the docstring of `isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness` before editing anything here: it
retracts a standing negative result of this lane, and the retraction is what makes the
corollaries possible. -/

variable (C) in
/-- **THE `IsSplitWitness` INTRODUCTION RULE — the one this lane recorded as impossible.**

A presenting Čech class over a finite separable `L`, plus a witness divisor inside it, gives
`IsSplitWitness`.  Nothing here mentions `θ`, `Σ` or a twist; the twisted case is the
corollary below.

**This RETRACTS the "no positional introduction rule exists" record** of
`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s closing note and of the memory item filed with it.  That
record was measured, and its measurement was right about what it tested — five variants, all
timing out at 1000000+ heartbeats:

* `exact`/`refine` with all twelve components as ONE anonymous constructor;
* the witness clause pre-bundled as a `have`;
* either curve spelling normalised to the other;
* `(isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness …).mpr` applied to the twelve-tuple;
* the trivial splitting `L := K`.

What none of them tested is **staging the existentials**.  Introducing them one at a time —
eight `Exists.intro`s and a four-component tail — costs nothing at the DEFAULT 200000
heartbeat budget.  The diagnosis the old record gives is still correct: the anonymous
constructor makes Lean unify the seven instance slots *while `L` is still a metavariable*,
re-checking `(relCurve C L).CechPic` against `((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor` on each
attempted assignment.  Staging fixes `L` at the first step, so every later component is
checked against a closed type and the two spellings never race.

**The transferable rule**, and it is stronger than the one it replaces: for a deep existential
over types-with-instances, `refine Exists.intro x ?_` repeatedly, rather than one tuple.  The
old advice ("restate the definition with one spelling") would have been a large refactor of a
co-signed definition; the actual fix is a tactic-level one.  Measured, not inferred: this
theorem's own body is the evidence, and the twisted corollary below consumes it. -/
theorem isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness
    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (ν : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
    [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
    (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K ν)
      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M))
    (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
    (hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M)
    (hW1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)) :
    IsSplitWitness C ν := by
  refine Exists.intro L ?_
  refine Exists.intro ‹Field L› ?_
  refine Exists.intro ‹Algebra k L› ?_
  refine Exists.intro ‹Algebra K L› ?_
  refine Exists.intro ‹IsScalarTower k K L› ?_
  refine Exists.intro ‹Module.Finite K L› ?_
  refine Exists.intro ‹Algebra.IsSeparable K L› ?_
  refine Exists.intro M ?_
  exact ⟨hM, W, hW, hW1⟩

variable (C) in
/-- **The TRIVIAL splitting `L := K`** — the variant the predecessor record singled out as
"worth wanting" and reported as unelaborable.

At a field where the class is *already* honest, no extension is needed: a witness divisor over
`K` itself certifies `IsSplitWitness`.  The record (I-0564) noted specifically that this one
"fails for elaboration reasons, NOT because the mathematics is wrong".  The mathematics was
indeed fine and the elaboration is fine too, once the existentials are staged — this is a
one-line corollary of the theorem above, at `L := K` with the identity instances.

Why it matters beyond closing a record: this is the **reverse half of
`IsChartDatumPresentation`**, the one residue CHART-U(b) still carries.  The forward half needs
a presenting datum's fibre predicate to imply the split predicate; that direction is the one
this supplies, since a datum over the base gives an honest class at the fibre field with no
extension to find. -/
theorem isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness_self
    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (ν : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (M : (relCurve C K).CechPic)
    (hM : PicEtAff.map C K (picEtAffineEquiv C K ν)
      = PicEtAff.unit C K (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M))
    (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left).CurveDivisor)
    (hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K W = M)
    (hW1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.divisorSheaf K W) 1)) :
    IsSplitWitness C ν :=
  isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness C ν M hM W hW hW1

variable (C) in
/-- **COV-1's introduction rule for `chartLocus` membership.**

Given, at the fibre field `K = κ(t)`:
* a finite separable `L/K` and a Čech class `M₀` presenting the *untwisted* fibre class `μ`;
* a divisor `W` on `C_L` whose class is `M₀ · (twist class base-changed to L)` and whose
  `H¹` vanishes,

the *twisted* class `μ · θ^m · Σ⁻¹` satisfies `IsSplitWitness`.  Both hypotheses are what
`w4-datb` §1.2 produces: the first at step 1 (`exists_splitting_of_picEt`), the second at
step 5 (the greedy drop of `RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean`) once step 3 has chosen `m`
against the fibre's own vanishing bound.

The twist is written in the `chartTwistClass` (collapsed) spelling, which is where the
degree bookkeeping happens; `chartTwist_eq_mul_thetaFamily_chartTwistClass` converts. -/
theorem isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass
    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
    [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
    (hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W
      = M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
    (hW1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)) :
    IsSplitWitness C (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C m Z) (overSpec k K)) :=
  isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness C _ _
    (picEtAffineEquiv_map_chartTwistFactor_eq_unit C μ M₀ hM₀ m Z) W hW hW1

end

4	---
5	
6	## Required proof loop
7	
8	Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
9	at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
10	`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
11	before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
12	search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.
13	
14	Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
15	check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
16	validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
17	unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
18	usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
19	the check.
20	
21	LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
22	module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
23	configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
24	the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
25	only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
26	specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.
27	
28	- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
29	  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
30	  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
31	- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
32	  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
33	  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
34	  project root.
35	- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
36	  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
37	- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
38	- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
39	  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
40	- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
41	  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.
42	
43	## Fast LSP proving loop
44	
45	The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
46	(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:
47	
48	- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
49	  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
50	- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
51	  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
52	- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
53	  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
54	  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
55	- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
56	  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
57	  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
58	  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.
59	
60	Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
61	skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
62	candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
63	kernel-check the module at the end.
64	
65	## Heavy builds — actually wait for them
66	
67	Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
68	deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
69	ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
70	or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
71	"Warnings are work").
72	
73	A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
74	most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
75	build to finish**:
76	
77	- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
78	  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
79	  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
80	  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
81	- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
82	  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
83	  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
84	  is *not* done.
85	- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
86	  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
87	  for final validation.
88	- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
89	  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
90	  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
91	  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
92	- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
93	  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
94	  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end

97	## When the LSP dies on big import files
98	
99	The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
100	imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
101	that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
102	run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
103	proof error:
104	
105	- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
106	  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
107	  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
108	- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
109	  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
110	  the specific module you are proving in instead.
111	- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
112	  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]

/-- The affine comparison intertwines the section-ring pullback along `Spec` of an
algebra map with the algebra map itself. -/
private lemma overSpecΓTop_appLE_comp (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) :
    (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k B).toAlgHom.comp
      (Over.appLEAlgHom (Over.overSpecMap φ) (overSpecTopAffine A).1
        (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top)
      = φ.comp (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom := by
  have key : (Over.overSpecMap φ).left.appLE (overSpecTopAffine A).1
        (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of B)).hom
      = (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).hom ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom := by
    have h₁ : (Over.overSpecMap φ).left.appLE (overSpecTopAffine A).1
          (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top
        = (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom)).appTop :=
      Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app _
    rw [h₁]
    exact Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom)
  ext x
  exact congr($(key).hom x)

/-- **Naturality of the affine comparison**: over affine tests, `picEtMap` along `Spec`
of an algebra map corresponds to `PicEtAff.mapAlg` under the comparison isomorphisms. -/
theorem picEtAffineEquiv_naturality (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) (s : picEt C (overSpec k A)) :
    picEtAffineEquiv C B (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap φ) s)
      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ (picEtAffineEquiv C A s) := by
  rw [picEtAffineEquiv_apply, picEtAffineEquiv_apply, picEtMap_val]
  have hval := picEtMapVal_eq_mapAlg C (Over.overSpecMap φ) s
    (W := overSpecTopAffine B) (V := overSpecTopAffine A) le_top
  rw [hval]
  calc PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k B).toAlgHom
        (PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.appLEAlgHom (Over.overSpecMap φ)
          (overSpecTopAffine A).1 (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top)
          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)))
      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C ((Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k B).toAlgHom.comp
          (Over.appLEAlgHom (Over.overSpecMap φ)
            (overSpecTopAffine A).1 (overSpecTopAffine B).1 le_top))
          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) := (PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp C _ _ _).symm
    _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (φ.comp (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom)
          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) := by
        rw [overSpecΓTop_appLE_comp φ]
        exact rfl
    _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ (PicEtAff.mapAlg C
          (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A))) :=
        PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp C _ _ _

end AffineNaturality

/-! ## Uniqueness of gluings for `picEt` itself -/

/-- **Uniqueness of gluings**: two sections of `picEt C T` agreeing on every affine open
subordinate to an open cover of `T.left` are equal — the separation half of the sheaf
property of the Layer-2 functor, the binding input of the (C2) comparison and the
degree interface. -/
theorem picEt.ext_of_le_cover {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {ι' : Type*}
    (O : ι' → T.left.Opens) (hcov : ∀ p : T.left, ∃ i, p ∈ O i) {s t : picEt C T}
    (h : ∀ (U : T.left.affineOpens) (i : ι'), U.1 ≤ O i → s.1 U = t.1 U) : s = t := by
  classical
  refine picEt.ext fun U => ?_
  obtain ⟨sub, hspan, hsub⟩ := Scheme.exists_basic_subcover U.2
    (fun U₀ => ∃ i, U₀ ≤ O i)
    (fun w _ => by
      obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hcov w
      exact ⟨O i, hi, ⟨i, le_rfl⟩⟩)
  refine picEt.eq_of_basic_eq C U sub hspan (fun r hr => ?_)
  obtain ⟨U₀, ⟨i, hle⟩, hrle⟩ := hsub r hr
  rw [s.compat ⟨_, U.2.basicOpen r⟩ U (T.left.basicOpen_le r),
    t.compat ⟨_, U.2.basicOpen r⟩ U (T.left.basicOpen_le r)]
  exact h ⟨T.left.basicOpen r, U.2.basicOpen r⟩ i (hrle.trans hle)

private lemma mapFun_mul (a b : PicEtAff C A) :
    mapFun C A' (a * b) = mapFun C A' a * mapFun C A' b := by
  induction a using ind with | _ E x =>
  induction b using ind with | _ F y =>
  have h₁ : mapFun C A' (mk C E x)
      = mk C ((E.prod F).baseChange A')
          (descentBaseChange C A' (E.prod F) (descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x)) := by
    rw [← mk_descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x, mapFun_mk]
  have h₂ : mapFun C A' (mk C F y)
      = mk C ((E.prod F).baseChange A')
          (descentBaseChange C A' (E.prod F) (descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y)) := by
    rw [← mk_descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y, mapFun_mk]
  rw [mk_mul_mk, mapFun_mk, map_mul, ← mk_mul_mk_same, h₁, h₂]

/-- Restriction of étale-plus Picard classes along a base extension `A → A'` of affine
tests: base-change the representing cover and transport the descent datum along the
canonical inclusion of the carrier into its base change. -/
def map : PicEtAff C A →* PicEtAff C A' :=
  MonoidHom.mk' (mapFun C A') (mapFun_mul C A')

@[simp]
lemma map_mk (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) :
    map C A' (mk C E x) = mk C (E.baseChange A') (descentBaseChange C A' E x) :=
  rfl

/-! ## Naturality of the unit and the functor laws -/

/-- The unit of the plus construction is natural in the test algebra. -/
theorem map_unit (x : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
    map C A' (unit C A x)
      = unit C A' (relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A') x) := by
  have hj : (((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k).comp
        ((Algebra.ofId A (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).Carrier).restrictScalars k)
      = ((((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A').fromSelf).restrictScalars k).comp
          (((Algebra.ofId A' (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A').Carrier).restrictScalars k).comp
            (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A')) := by
    ext a
    simp only [AlgHom.coe_comp, AlgHom.coe_restrictScalars', Function.comp_apply,
      Algebra.ofId_apply, IsScalarTower.coe_toAlgHom', AlgHom.commutes]
    exact IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply A A' _ a
  have hval : relPicAlgMap C
        (((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChangeInclude A').restrictScalars k)
        (relPicAlgMap C
          ((Algebra.ofId A (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).Carrier).restrictScalars k) x)
      = relPicAlgMap C
          ((((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A').fromSelf).restrictScalars k)
          (relPicAlgMap C
            ((Algebra.ofId A' (Algebra.EtaleCover.self A').Carrier).restrictScalars k)
            (relPicAlgMap C (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A A') x)) := by
    rw [← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, hj,
      AlgHom.comp_assoc]
  calc map C A' (unit C A x)
      = mk C ((Algebra.EtaleCover.self A).baseChange A')

def testPointFieldAlgHom {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left) :
    testPointField (T := T) (f.left.base t) →ₐ[k] testPointField (T := T') t :=
  { (testPointFieldMap f t).hom with
    commutes' := fun r => congrFun (congrArg DFunLike.coe
      (testPointFieldMap_comp_algebraMap f t)) r }

/-- When the extension is invertible it is a `k`-algebra equivalence. -/
def testPointFieldAlgEquiv {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left)
    [IsIso (testPointFieldMap f t)] :
    testPointField (T := T) (f.left.base t) ≃ₐ[k] testPointField (T := T') t :=
  { (asIso (testPointFieldMap f t)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv with
    commutes' := (testPointFieldAlgHom f t).commutes }
